title: Technician Role & Maintenance Fundamentals
contentStatus: PROPOSED title/content, pending DiFacto confirmation. Drafted from CDD role mapping (L3A = Maintenance Technician track) and general industrial maintenance practice. Specific DiFacto procedures pending SME input.

sections.title: From Operator to Technician
learningObjectives: Understand how the Technician role differs from the Operator role
Recognize the scope of responsibility this track covers
sections.content: L1-L2 built operational competence - running MoRo day to day, recognizing issues, escalating appropriately. The Technician track goes further: you're now the person issues get escalated to. This track covers maintaining MoRo's physical and operational health over its working life, not just operating it reliably day to day.

keyTerms.note: A robot that navigates autonomously using sensor-based awareness — the category MoRo belongs to.

sections.title: Categories of Maintenance Work
learningObjectives: Distinguish between preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance
Understand why a mix of approaches is used rather than one alone
sections.content: Maintenance work generally falls into three categories: preventive (scheduled work done regardless of current condition, to prevent failure), predictive (work triggered by signs of degradation before failure occurs), and corrective (fixing something after it's already failed). A mature maintenance program relies primarily on preventive and predictive work, with corrective maintenance treated as the exception rather than the norm.

keyTerms.note: Scheduled maintenance performed regardless of current condition, to prevent future failure.
Maintenance triggered by observed signs of degradation, performed before failure occurs.
Maintenance performed after a failure has already occurred.

sections.title: MoRo's Maintainable Components
learningObjectives: Identify the general categories of components a Technician maintains
Understand why each category requires different maintenance approaches
sections.content: MoRo's maintainable scope spans several categories: mechanical (wheels, drive components, physical structure), sensing (LiDAR and related sensors), power (battery and charging systems), and software/firmware (periodic updates). Each category has different failure patterns and different maintenance cadences - mechanical wear is gradual and often predictable, while software issues tend to be more binary (working or not).

sections.title: Reading Maintenance Documentation
learningObjectives: Understand the role of maintenance records in technician work
Know what a complete maintenance record typically includes
sections.content: Every maintenance action - preventive, predictive, or corrective - should be documented: what was done, when, and why. This record is what makes future maintenance smarter over time, since patterns across a unit's history (or across the fleet) often reveal issues that a single maintenance event wouldn't show on its own.

sections.title: Safety During Maintenance Work
learningObjectives: Understand how safety procedures during maintenance differ from operational safety
Recognize lockout/tagout as a foundational maintenance safety practice
sections.content: Maintenance work often requires MoRo to be powered down or placed in a state where it won't move unexpectedly while being worked on - lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures exist specifically for this. Unlike operational safety (staying clear of an active unit), maintenance safety is about confirming a unit is genuinely de-energized and locked out before physical work begins. Specific LOTO procedures for MoRo will be confirmed against DiFacto's safety documentation.

keyTerms.note: A safety procedure confirming equipment is de-energized and physically secured before maintenance work begins.

sections.title: What This Track Builds Toward
learningObjectives: Understand the progression through the remaining L3A modules
Recognize the certification this track leads to
sections.content: This module establishes the foundation; subsequent L3A modules build specific competency in preventive procedures, predictive inspection, battery diagnostics, diagnostic methodology, and troubleshooting - culminating in the field drill capstone. Together, these complete the requirements for DiFacto Certified IMR Technician status.

questions.question: What distinguishes the Technician role from the Operator role?
options: Technicians maintain MoRo's physical and operational health over time, beyond day-to-day operation
questions.feedback: Correct. The Technician track covers maintenance responsibility beyond operational competence.

questions.question: What are the three general categories of maintenance work?
questions.feedback: Correct. These three categories describe different triggers for maintenance action.

questions.question: Should a mature maintenance program rely primarily on corrective maintenance?
options: Yes, fixing things after they fail is most efficient
No - preventive and predictive work should be primary, with corrective as the exception
questions.feedback: Correct. Relying mainly on preventive and predictive maintenance reduces unplanned failures.

questions.question: Why does documentation matter for maintenance work?
options: Patterns across maintenance history reveal issues a single event wouldn't show
It's only needed for warranty claims
It's just a formality with no real value
questions.feedback: Correct. Documentation builds a pattern history that improves future maintenance decisions.

questions.question: What is lockout/tagout (LOTO) primarily for?
options: Confirming a unit is de-energized and secured before physical maintenance work begins
questions.feedback: Correct. LOTO ensures a unit won't move unexpectedly while being physically worked on.
